---
title: "Karlsruhe is getting warmer"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
p_load(tidyverse)

yearly <- read_csv("data/weather_karlsruhe.csv") |>
  group_by(year = year(date)) |>
  summarize(
    temp_mean = mean(temp_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_days = n()
  ) |>
  filter(n_days >= 360)
```

This small website uses daily weather data for Karlsruhe since 1876 from
[@dwd2026](references.qmd#ref-dwd2026). It has three pages: this one, [Hot and frost days](days.qmd), and
[Explore](explore.qmd). All sources are listed on the [References](references.qmd) page.

## Annual temperature

@fig-anomaly shows how much warmer or colder each year was than the 1961–1990 mean.

```{r}
#| label: fig-anomaly
#| fig-cap: "Annual mean temperature in Karlsruhe, deviation from the 1961–1990 mean."
reference_mean <- yearly |>
  filter(year %in% 1961:1990) |>
  pull(temp_mean) |>
  mean()

yearly |>
  mutate(anomaly = temp_mean - reference_mean) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = anomaly, fill = anomaly)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "grey90", high = "firebrick", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Deviation (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The warming also shows in the extremes: hot days have become more frequent
([the hot-days figure](days.qmd#fig-days) on the next page), and you can explore every single year interactively in the
[plotly figure on the Explore page](explore.qmd#fig-explore). The colours follow the idea of the warming stripes by
[@hawkins2018](references.qmd#ref-hawkins2018).
